I do have $500 on me, but I'd like to ask some questions before I come down and take a proper look. I did some googling about what maintenance or repair work that needs to be done on any bike that's been sitting to make it like-new.

Did you change the grease and ball bearings (headset, front hub) from it having dried out, and if so, who did the rebuild/overhaul work? I probably know them, but there are some guys who tend to use Park's grease instead of Marine Grease, and I find that it tends to run a bit thick for longer wear purposes.

Did you or the prior owner add 5w30 motor oil into the rear hub (1tb every week)? How old is the indicator chain, what is its material, and who made it? How old are the spokes and who built the (assumedly, at $500, it was a custom build) wheel up?

The best steel is Chromoly Steel, and it's stronger, more resilient to impact than the cheaper, "Hi Tensile" steel bikes of the era. Since Chromoly steel is stronger, builders could get away with using less material, therefore saving weight and making the bike more responsive but just as strong. The practice continued into aluminum and carbon fiber, as well, but manufacturers began referring to the process as "drawing." (So if I've lost you here, maybe that will help?)
